evidence: src/application/require-order.ts: requireOrder is the single place that throws DomainError('not_found'); advance-order-use-case.ts, cancel-order-use-case.ts and get-order-use-case.ts all call it.
src/application/order-dto.ts: toOrderDto is the single Order->OrderDto mapper, used by Advance, Cancel, Get, ListOrdersByState and Place use cases.
src/application/place-order-use-case.ts and cancel-order-use-case.ts delegate to reserveStock/releaseStock from the domain instead of duplicating stock logic.
src/application/list-orders-by-state-use-case.ts: the isOrderState validation exists only here, with no duplicate elsewhere in the module.
Minor: StockLevelDto is in order-dto.ts and list-stock-levels-use-case.ts maps inline, not through a toStockLevelDto function; this is not enough to fail.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module is one cohesive application layer for order fulfilment. Each file is either a use case or a shared helper. The use cases are consistent: constructor-injected repository ports, an `execute` method, and `OrderDto` as the return type. The "order not found" rule lives only in `requireOrder`, and Advance, Cancel and Get all use it. Mapping from `Order` to DTO lives only in `toOrderDto`, and every order-returning use case calls it. Stock reserve and release rules are delegated to the domain functions `reserveStock` and `releaseStock`, not reimplemented. Unknown-state validation appears only in `ListOrdersByStateUseCase`, so it is not duplicated. Two minor smells do not amount to a split, duplication or bypass. `StockLevelDto` sits in `order-dto.ts`, and `ListStockLevelsUseCase` maps inline instead of through a mapper function.
